## The first week's reports, and four bugs nobody reported

Everything here started as a message from a server owner running 2.0.1 — the inspect card fighting the jam animation, officers carrying two pistols, a confirmation prompt some servers never wanted. Working through those turned up four more problems that had been shipping quietly, including one that was losing saved settings.

### New

- **The holster confirmation can be turned off.** Dashboard → General → *Holster Confirm*. The draw animation still plays; it just stops waiting for an answer. QBCore owners already had a way out through `QBWeapons.SidearmDrawMode`; `ox_inventory` owners had none short of disabling the sling entirely. Takes effect immediately, no restart.
- **Hide weapons per job.** Police uniforms — GTA's own and most EUP packs — have a duty holster with a pistol modelled into the clothing, so an officer wearing one ended up carrying two. `MBT.HiddenByJob` in `config.lua` stops us adding ours. The job `'*'` means everyone, for servers that never want a pistol on the hip at all. It re-evaluates the moment someone changes job, for everyone who can see them.
- **Every keybind now lives in `config.lua`**, in one block. They were scattered across a thousand lines of `default.lua`. See the note below if you keep your own config file.
- **`/mbt_slingdebug`** on debug builds prints, per body slot, whether a prop exists and why it is or isn't hidden. For the support conversation that starts with "the pistol still shows".

### Fixed

- **Inspecting a jammed weapon.** The jam loop replays its animation every 800ms, so starting an inspect on top of it put two animations on the same ped, fighting. Inspect now refuses to start while jammed, and an inspect already running ends if a jam happens mid-look.
- **An inspect that never let go.** Inspect ends on key *release*. If the same key opens your inventory, the inventory takes focus on key-down and the release never reaches the game, leaving the card up until you pressed again. It now gives up after fifteen seconds. The real fix is still rebinding the key, which is now easy to find.
- **Job checks failing at random on ox_core.** The bridge picked one group out of however many a player held, using an iteration order Lua does not define — so the same player could pass or fail the same check from one call to the next. This affected the armoury gate, pat-down permission, casing examine and weapon naming, not just the new feature. ESX, QBCore and QBox have a single job and were never exposed.
- **Slung weapons ignoring a job change.** Nothing re-evaluated when a player changed job, so props kept whatever they were given when they spawned. This also fixes per-job position overrides, which never re-applied either.
- **Per-job sling variants disappearing on restart.** Saved dashboard settings are merged over the live defaults, and that merge walked the defaults' keys — which for a map keyed by your own job names is an empty table. The saved entries were dropped every boot. **If you set per-job sling variants and found them reset, this is why.**
- **Attachments on servers behind an inventory shim.** We read `ox_inventory`'s weapon data file directly, because that is where suppressor and flashlight definitions live. A resource that forwards ox's exports without shipping that file left us with nothing, and suppressor heat switched itself off. It now falls back to our own bundled copy.
- **Drawing a long gun took two full seconds** against 400ms for a pistol. Now 1200ms, which still lets the reach-behind animation finish.

### Note for server owners

**If you update by replacing the whole folder, there is nothing to do.**

If you keep your own `config.lua` instead, copy the **Keybinds** block out of the new one — your file predates it, and without it every key ends up unassigned. The script says so in the console on startup rather than leaving you guessing. Every feature keeps its chat command in the meantime.

While you are in there: `MBT.HiddenByJob` is in the same file, and it is the fix for officers carrying two pistols.

### Install

Download `mbt_malisling.zip` below and drop it in your resources folder. Existing 2.0.x installs upgrade in place — dashboard settings, placed racks, trunk contents and saved positions are all kept.

The `ox_inventory` patch is re-applied automatically on first start: this release changes it, and the installer now notices when the copy inside `ox_inventory` is older and rewrites it from its own backup.

> **Coming from 1.x?** Replace the whole folder and do **not** keep your old `config.lua`. It opens with `MBT = {}` and loads after `default.lua`, so keeping it wipes the new defaults and the script won't start. Feature tuning moved into the dashboard — set it again in game, and it persists to the database from then on.
